name: Northern Dipper
source: Sancai Tuhui (1609), Qiyong (implements) chapter 12, household utensils, plate '熨斗 (flat-iron pan)'; National Diet Library copy 三才圖會 106卷 [16], frame 39
treatment: genuine cut-out: a pan with a key-fret band and a long straight handle from a dragon-head socket
fit: similarity (scale, turn, shift) on named picture points, mirrored (no writing in the cut)
subject: 北斗, the Northern Dipper: the encyclopaedia's 熨斗, a pan-shaped 斗 with a straight handle
honesty: A flat-iron pan (熨斗), not a wine ladle; mirrored so that its handle runs east like the Dipper's. Its handle is straight; the Dipper's bends at Mizar.
subject_role_note: the group's name is a ladle (斗); the plate is the 熨斗, a 斗-shaped pan with a long handle (a flat-iron), the closest straight-handled 斗 found
